# Papers on speech emotion recognition, emotional TTS, urban flow and OD demand prediction, and hyperspectral image classification

> Paper pages with verified summaries, quick facts, quoted results, abstracts, FAQs and BibTeX. Topics: speech emotion recognition, emotion-controllable text-to-speech for diffusion and flow-matching models, urban flow prediction, origin-destination demand prediction, hyperspectral image classification.

Preferred citation: the BibTeX on each paper page or at https://codezx6.github.io/publications.bib.

## Topic overviews

- [Speech emotion recognition and emotional text-to-speech for humanoid robots](https://codezx6.github.io/topics/speech-emotion.html): Two 2026 arXiv papers address both directions of affective speech: recognising emotion in speech (PhysioSER; Zhang et al., 2026) and generating emotional speech (DUET; Zhang et al., 2026). Both methods are designed as plug-and-play frameworks that keep the pretrained model frozen, and both were deployed on a humanoid robot.
- [Urban flow prediction with masked and contrastive spatio-temporal pre-training](https://codezx6.github.io/topics/urban-flow-prediction.html): Urban flow prediction forecasts future flows across city regions from historical flow data and supports services such as trip planning, congestion control, and public safety. Three papers (Zhang et al., CIKM 2023; Zhang et al., Knowledge-Based Systems 2023; Zhang et al., Neural Networks 2025) develop self-supervised spatio-temporal pre-training for this task.
- [Origin-destination (OD) flow and demand prediction for metro and taxi systems](https://codezx6.github.io/topics/origin-destination-prediction.html): Origin-destination (OD) prediction forecasts the flow or demand between pairs of stations or regions, which supports real-time traffic management, vehicle dispatch, and resource allocation in intelligent transportation systems. Two papers (Yu et al., Expert Systems with Applications 2025; Gong et al., Expert Systems with Applications 2026) study this problem on metro and taxi data.
- [Hyperspectral image classification: cross-domain few-shot learning and superpixel mutual enhancement](https://codezx6.github.io/topics/hyperspectral-image-classification.html): Two IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing papers (Cao et al., 2024; Cao et al., 2025) study hyperspectral image (HSI) classification.
- [中文论文索引](https://codezx6.github.io/zh/): Chinese titles and summaries of every paper

## Papers

- [DUET: Unified Dual-Space Emotion Control for Diffusion and Flow-Matching Driven Text-to-Speech](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/duet.html): Xu Zhang, Longbing Cao, Zhangkai Wu. arXiv:2606.00066 (2026). DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2606.00066. DUET adds emotion control to frozen diffusion and flow-matching TTS models by steering hidden states along a linearly decodable emotion direction and refining the mel estimate with emotion-recognizer gradients passed through a differentiable vocoder. With GradTTS on ESD it reaches 75.5% average emotion accuracy (strongest supervised baseline: 46.8%).
- [PhysioSER: Learning Physiology-Informed Vocal Spectrotemporal Representations for Speech Emotion Recognition](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/physioser.html): Xu Zhang, Longbing Cao, Runze Yang, Zhangkai Wu. arXiv:2602.13259 (2026). DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2602.13259. PhysioSER complements a frozen self-supervised (SSL) backbone with a compact physiology-informed branch that encodes vocal amplitude and phase features with quaternion convolutions, for speech emotion recognition. With frozen WavLM on CREMA-D, it raises weighted accuracy from 69.69% to 75.20%.
- [DSTCN: Exploiting dynamic spatio-temporal correlations for origin-destination demand prediction](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/dstcn.html): Yongshun Gong, Piao Yu, Xu Zhang, Xinxin Zhang, Xiushan Nie, Haoliang Sun. Expert Systems with Applications, vol. 299, article 130095 (2026). DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2025.130095. DSTCN (Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Correlation Network) forecasts origin-destination demand matrices with three modules: Glstm2D for origin- and destination-side demand trends, Simformer for Transformer-based spatial similarity across the OD matrix, and FF-TM for feature fusion and temporal modeling. On NYC-TOD2018 its MAE of 1.469 is 3.04% below the best baseline.
- [S2CMEN: A Mutually Enhancement Network for Superpixel Segmentation and Classification of Hyperspectral Image](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mutual-enhancement-hsi.html): Mengxin Cao, Yongmin Li, Xu Zhang, Guixin Zhao, Guohua Lv, Aimei Dong, Jinyong Cheng, Wei Li, Xiangjun Dong. IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, vol. 63, article 5524714 (2025). DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2025.3608942. S²CMEN (S2CMEN) is a hyperspectral image classification network in which superpixel segmentation and classification enhance each other through a unified loss, combining superpixel-based global spatial context with Spectral-Swin Transformer spectral features. It reaches 97.38% overall accuracy on Indian Pines.
- [MR-UFP: Enhancing urban flow prediction via mutual reinforcement with multi-scale regional information](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mr-ufp.html): Xu Zhang, Mengxin Cao, Yongshun Gong, Xiaoming Wu, Xiangjun Dong, Ying Guo, Long Zhao, Chengqi Zhang. Neural Networks, vol. 182, article 106900 (2025). DOI 10.1016/j.neunet.2024.106900. MR-UFP predicts the inflow and outflow of city grid regions, even with limited training data, by pre-training encoders with spatial-temporal masking and contrastive learning and training flow prediction jointly with a multi-scale region-classification task. On full TaxiBJ and BikeNYC it beats all 13 baselines (RMSE 14.32 and 4.45).
- [BiST-IF: Enhancing origin–destination flow prediction via bi-directional spatio-temporal inference and interconnected feature evolution](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/bist-if.html): Piao Yu, Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Jian Zhang, Haoliang Sun, Junjie Zhang, Xinxin Zhang, Yilong Yin. Expert Systems with Applications, vol. 264, article 125679 (2025). DOI 10.1016/j.eswa.2024.125679. BiST-IF predicts origin–destination (OD) flows between metro stations or urban areas by correcting delayed recent OD matrices, applying bi-directional origin/destination attention, and fusing arrival-side (Out-OD) flows through an attention-based mutual information mechanism. It lowers MAE by an average of 7.55% on HZMetro relative to the best baseline.
- [Automatic visual recognition for leaf disease based on enhanced attention mechanism](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/leaf-disease-attention.html): Yumeng Yao, Xiaodun Deng, Xu Zhang, Junming Li, Wenxuan Sun, Gechao Zhang. PeerJ Computer Science, vol. 10, article e2365 (2024). DOI 10.7717/peerj-cs.2365. A tomato leaf disease detector that adds the DyHead attention module to YOLOv4-tiny and trains it with a Focaler-SIoU box loss. On PlantDoc tomato leaf images it reaches 93.64% mAP, 10.3 percentage points above the YOLOv4-tiny baseline.
- [S3CFSL: Spatial-Spectral–Semantic Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning for Hyperspectral Image Classification](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/spatial-spectral-semantic-fsl.html): Mengxin Cao, Xu Zhang, Jinyong Cheng, Guixin Zhao, Wei Li, Xiangjun Dong. IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing, vol. 62, article 5525315 (2024). DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2024.3434484. S3CFSL classifies new hyperspectral scenes from five labelled samples per class by transferring knowledge from the labelled Chikusei scene. It combines a cross-spatial–spectral transformer, Gaussian feature denoising and semantic-enhanced domain alignment, and reports 98.52% overall accuracy on Pavia Centre, 88.79% on Salinas and 77.63% on Houston.
- [ST-FCL: Spatio-temporal fusion and contrastive learning for urban flow prediction](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/st-csl.html): Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Chengqi Zhang, Xiaoming Wu, Ying Guo, Wenpeng Lu, Long Zhao, Xiangjun Dong. Knowledge-Based Systems, vol. 282, article 111104 (2023). DOI 10.1016/j.knosys.2023.111104. ST-FCL predicts grid-level urban inflow and outflow by fusing temporal and spatial views, learned through contrastive pretraining, with an external-factor view. On the full TaxiBJ dataset it reaches RMSE 14.71, against 15.41 for the best baseline, ATFM.
- [MC-STL: Mask- and Contrast-Enhanced Spatio-Temporal Learning for Urban Flow Prediction](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/mcstl.html): Xu Zhang, Yongshun Gong, Xinxin Zhang, Xiaoming Wu, Chengqi Zhang, Xiangjun Dong. CIKM 2023, pp. 3298–3307. DOI 10.1145/3583780.3614958. MC-STL pre-trains two encoders for urban flow prediction: a ViT encoder learns to reconstruct regions masked at different timestamps, and its attention weights also build a GCN adjacency matrix; a global-local cross-attention encoder learns a temporal-order contrastive task. It reaches RMSE 14.53 on full TaxiBJ.
- [URMDet-SimFire: Trustworthy multimodal detection with uncertainty and reliability modeling for fire and smoke analytics](https://codezx6.github.io/papers/urmdet-simfire.html): Zhonghua Dang, Xu Zhang. Array, vol. 31, article 101124 (2026). DOI 10.1016/j.array.2026.101124. URMDet-SimFire is an uncertainty- and reliability-aware multimodal object detection framework for fire and smoke that reweights each input modality by its estimated reliability and calibrates each detection's confidence by its uncertainty. In simulation only, it raised F1 from 0.4348 (vision-only baseline) to 0.4638.
